content.text:
I've now inspected every responsive location. My conclusions:

- **§ 2(a) Grant (p0022/p0024)** — the licence scope words ("in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables") delimit only our permitted use of *TrueLink's* Interface; they do not restrict what business we may operate. The very next sentence is an affirmative pro-Customer freedom-to-compete covenant: we may acquire, develop, license or otherwise use any competing software or services (subject only to non-infringement of TrueLink IP and our confidentiality obligations).
- **§ 8 Covenants of Client (p0051–p0058)** — contains only compliance, notification, access-control, content warranty and anti-spam covenants; no restrictive covenant.
- **§ 8(d) (p0054)** — the only "non-compete" reference; it operates as a *limitation on TrueLink's* licence to exploit our Credit Data, so it runs in our favour.
- **§§ 7, 10, 12–30** — no field-of-use, territory, exclusivity or minimum-purchase restriction binding us.

No redline is warranted.

input.quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us, so it sits at the preferred position and needs no redline. § 2(a) goes further and affirmatively preserves our freedom to buy or build: we are "not obligated to utilize the License" and are "free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink," qualified only by non-infringement of TrueLink IP (p0024) and our existing § 10 confidentiality obligations — both ordinary and not business restrictions. The § 2(a) grant language limiting use of the Interface to "the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables" is a scope-of-licence limit on our use of TrueLink's product, not a covenant about the businesses we may operate or the products we may procure, so it is not a field-of-use restriction of the kind this rule targets. § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) contains only compliance, notification, access-control, content and anti-spam covenants, and §§ 7 and 10–30 contain no exclusivity, territory or minimum-commitment restriction. The sole "non-competition" reference, in § 8(d), makes our Credit Data licence to TrueLink "subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement" — that operates as a restraint on TrueLink's exploitation of our data and therefore benefits us, so it is not flagged. Two drafting notes for diligence rather than redline points: the "Non-Competition Agreement" is referenced but neither defined nor attached, and we should confirm on execution that it imposes no covenant on Mortgage Logic's own mortgage or web businesses; if it does, this rule would need to be re-run against that document.
